Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg. EDSA corner Mapagmahal Street, Diliman, Quezon City DILG OPINION NO. April 16, 2010 VICE-MAYOR APOLINAR R. MARTINEZ Municipality of Pagbilao Province of Quezon Dear Vice-Mayor Martinez: 49 S. 2010 This concerns your letter-query seeking the legal opinion of this Department on who between the Municipal Mayor and Vice-Mayor has the power or authority to appoint the Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan. In response thereto, please be informed that we have already answered a similar query in DILG Opinion No. 67, series of 2004 dated August 23, 2004 that the power to appoint the Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan is vested with the Municipal Vice-Mayor. To date, we find no cogent reason to divert from or set aside the said opinion. Fof your ready reference, we are enclosing herewith a photocopy of said DILG opinion. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. JESUS B. DOQUE IV Director III, Legal Service Encl.: As stated. Legal: 28/ Merle

REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF SECRETARY opinion No. 67, s. 2004 August 23, 2004 ATTY. BENJIE Y. BAGUIO Kapatagan, Lanao del Norte Dear Sir: This refers to your letter-query regarding the issue as to who between the Municipal Mayor and the Vice-Mayor has the power or authority to appoint the Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan in case such position is to be filled up. In reply thereto, we answer that the power to appoint the Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan is vested with the Municipal Vice-Mayor. The Civil Service Commission, the central personnel agency of the government, came up with attached for ready reference), wherein, in interpreting Section 469 (a) of the Local Government Code (RA 7160), the Commission categorically declared that the Secretary to the Sangguniang bayan is not a department head but only an official of the sanggunian holding the rank and salary equal to that of a department head. It is then clear that it is the Vice-Mayor who has the power to appoint a nominee to the said office. To support this, the provision of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), insofar as pertinent provides that: "Section 445 (a) The Vice-Mayor shall: xxx xxx xxx (2) subject to civil service law, rules and regulations, appoint all OFFICIALS and employees of the sangguniang bayan, except those whose manner of appointment is specifically provided in this code; (underscoring ours). Section 443 (d) in relation with Section 469 (a) of RA 7160 cannot be made then to apply to the issue at hand because of the aforesaid CSC position of a Sangguniang Bayan Secretary. Section 469 (a) of RA 7160 merely provided that the Sangguniang Bayan Secretary shall have a rank and salary equal to that of a department head, and never classified the same position as a Department Head that calls for the exercise of the Mayor's power of appointment. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, ANGELO T. REYES Secretary DIR. RENE K.
